title: Chapter 53
content:
Chairman Kang stared intently at the black flash drive resting on his mahogany desk.

It had arrived via private courier on the exact day Kang Il-hyun was gunned down at the podium. Stored within its memory was covert surveillance footage from an overseas junket years ago, where he and several high-ranking lawmakers had partaken in illicit pleasures with an underage girl.

If the file ever leaked, Chairman Kang wouldn't be the only one destroyed. The latter half of the recording captured the entire party degenerating into a chaotic, tangled orgy. Had Kang Il-hyun kept a secondary copy for himself? Or had Lee Ja-kyeong?

Judging by the fact that the sniper had put two rounds through Il-hyun’s thighs rather than piercing his heart, an unsanctioned, covert bargain had almost certainly been struck behind his back.

Chairman Kang had deployed a hit squad to eliminate the assassin the moment the shot was fired, but the operative had evaporated into thin air. Still, if the kid valued his life, he would never dare step foot on Korean soil again. A quiet reconnaissance sweep confirmed that the secluded villa where Il-hyun had kept the boy was already swept completely bare.

Word had also reached him that afternoon that Il-hyun had been quietly transferred to an undisclosed medical facility. Chairman Kang chose to feign ignorance; with Kang Yu-jung already clued in and baring her fangs, stirring the pot any further would only invite unnecessary complications.

A crisp knock at the door broke the silence as three guests were ushered inside.

They were senior managing directors who had been instrumental in founding the conglomerate—the surviving three of the original four founding partners. When the fourth had turned traitor, Chairman Kang had dispatched Il-hyun to quietly erase him from existence.

The three directors settled into the armchairs as a secretary poured hot tea.

"Knowing the heavy grief you must be carrying, Chairman, we came to pay our respects and offer our humble condolences."

They presented a joint gift wrapped in an elaborate gold-silk cloth. The Chairman signaled for his secretary to take the parcel into the adjoining room.

"I am grateful that you would show such consideration for an old man."

"Who could have imagined such an atrocity would unfold at a formal inauguration ceremony?"

"I was thoroughly shaken myself, sir. Look at my hands—they still tremble at the thought."

Watching Director Park feign a delicate tremor in his fingers, Chairman Kang felt a wave of cold contempt wash over him. Back in your twenties, you butchered rivals with meat cleavers without batting an eye, and now you sit here playing the refined gentleman.

Taking a slow sip of tea, Chairman Kang watched as Director Kim—who had remained tactfully quiet—cast a calculating glance around the room before clearing his throat.

"While you must be bearing the brunt of the worry, Chairman, none of us have slept a wink either. Whispers are already spreading like wildfire among major institutional shareholders. Stock prices are tumbling, and talk is mounting that this tragedy only cements the company's image as a glorified syndicate."

"Director Kim speaks the truth," chimed the second. "Frankly speaking, I always anticipated something like this would happen one day. Given Executive Director Kang’s reckless, combative methods, it would be a miracle if he didn't have a legion of enemies out for blood. The board only held its tongue out of fear, but everyone harbored the exact same misgivings."

"Indeed. The executive roster has been nursing grievances for a long time. They simply couldn't voice them because you favored the boy so openly, Chairman... But in all honesty, he never possessed the temperament to succeed you. Most of the leadership agrees. Wouldn't you say so, gentlemen?"

"Foreign investors may favor his aggressive expansion strategies, but from where we stand, he is a liability destined to invite catastrophe. And when that storm breaks, the conglomerate will be forced to shoulder the ruin. Surely, Chairman, that is not an outcome you desire."

"Quite right, quite right."

The three men nodded in synchronized harmony, trading supportive murmurs.

Chairman Kang clipped a cigar, leaned his head back against the leather sofa, and studied the trio through hooded eyes. Despite their timid posturing, their intent was transparent: they intended to use this window to permanently purge Kang Il-hyun from the corporate hierarchy.

Exhaling a long ribbon of aromatic blue smoke, Chairman Kang spoke in a measured tone. "Then whom do you propose as the rightful successor?"

Sensing their opening, the three directors exchanged subtle glances before Director Kim took the lead.

"Director Kang Tae-han is the most natural fit. He is the eldest legitimate son, backed by a powerful maternal lineage, and he would never defy your grand vision, Chairman."

"Though Director Tae-han may appear a bit straightforward on the surface, he is far more pliable and receptive to counsel than Executive Director Kang ever was."

Twirling the cigar between his knuckles, Chairman Kang casually floated a probe to the three vipers.

"And what of Seok-joo?"

All three men shook their heads in immediate unison.

"The boy is far too young. It would be wiser for Seok-joo to join the company at a junior rank and learn the operations step-by-step."

"I concur. Seok-joo inherited your sharp intellect and the Madam's grace, so he will undoubtedly thrive in time. For now, let him enjoy his youth, and we can revisit the matter later."

To them, Kang Seok-joo was an utter nonentity.

"If that is the consensus of the founding board," Chairman Kang said slowly, "I shall take it under consideration."

Hearing the favorable response, the three directors couldn't suppress the triumphant gleam in their eyes.

Chairman Kang ground the ash from his cigar against the crystal tray, a ghost of a smile touching his lips. Armed with his tacit approval, these three would spend the coming days rallying institutional shareholders and board members to crown Kang Tae-han.

With Kang Il-hyun pinned to a hospital bed, they believed their golden hour had finally arrived.

Before stepping out of the sedan, Kim Sun-young leaned over to inspect Seok-joo’s suit one last time. Cupping her son’s chin, she looked him over with a radiant, ambitious smile.

Seok-joo merely slumped against the door, tapping away at his mobile phone with a bored scowl. She gave his shoulder a sharp, stinging slap.

"Straighten up! Make sure you leave an immaculate impression on the board today."

Seok-joo yanked at his collar with a groan. "Do I really have to be here?"

"Of course you do! Don't you want to watch with your own eyes as Kang Il-hyun’s head rolls off the corporate block?"

Seok-joo rolled his eyes. The man was locked away in a hospital bed, so seeing his face was out of the question, but the unfolding palace coup promised decent entertainment nonetheless.

The motorcade drew up before Haewon Group's global headquarters. Seok-joo and Kim Sun-young stepped out, accompanied by an entourage of executive secretaries, ascending to the high-level boardroom. Board members and major shareholders were already milling about, exchanging low-voiced pleasantries as they filed through the double doors.

Chairman Kang was seated dead-center at the head of the long conference table, flanked on his right by Kang Tae-han and his supporting faction.

Today's extraordinary general meeting had been convened with a singular, historic agenda: the formal motion to strip Kang Il-hyun of his title as Executive Director.

As Kim Sun-young entered, senior executives stood and bowed with deep deference. She took her seat directly to Chairman Kang's left.

While Director Kim, presiding as chairman of the meeting, delivered his opening remarks outlining the agenda, Seok-joo kept his phone hidden beneath the table, trading rapid-fire messages with his circle:

[Can't make it today. Stuck in the emergency board meeting. Today is the day Kang Il-hyun gets publicly executed!]

[For real? Does that mean you're stepping up as Executive Director?]

[Are you braindead? Why would I want a director title when I can hold out for the presidency?]

[Is Il-hyun officially unemployed now?]

[Looking at the room, Father has completely cut him loose lol]

"We shall now proceed to the formal vote on the primary agenda item: the resolution for the dismissal of Executive Director Kang Il-hyun."

Director Kim raised the wooden gavel, preparing to strike the block—

Bang.

The heavy double doors of the boardroom swung open.

A collective gasp rippled through the room as an entirely unexpected figure stepped through the threshold: Kang Yu-jung. Having virtually never attended a corporate shareholder assembly in her life, every pair of eyes locked onto her.

And then, the real shock rolled in behind her.

Navigating through the doorway in a high-grade mechanical wheelchair was Kang Il-hyun.

Dressed in loose hospital linens beneath dark designer sunglasses, his forearms were hooked to a mobile IV pole carrying bags of saline and analgesics.

The boardroom descended into absolute turmoil.

I thought he was dead. Wasn't he in an irreversible coma? What is happening? He looks completely coherent.

As shareholders erupted in frantic murmurs, Chairman Kang, Kim Sun-young, and Tae-han froze in pure, petrified shock.

Park Tae-soo stepped forward, smoothly pulling out a leather chair in the second row directly behind Chairman Kang to slide Il-hyun’s wheelchair into place. Director Kwon, seated immediately to the right, leaned in with urgent, hushed concern.

"Director Kang... Are you truly well enough to be here? You have no idea the terror we felt that day."

Kwon was one of Il-hyun’s long-standing loyalists on the board. Several other sympathetic executives quickly leaned in, murmuring about the catastrophic rumors that had plagued the markets.

Il-hyun slid his dark glasses down the bridge of his nose, offering a thin, razor-sharp smile.

"I am quite well, gentlemen. Though as you can see, I am relegated to this wheelchair for the time being."

With the room’s undivided attention pinned squarely on him, Il-hyun raised a single hand toward Director Kim at the podium.

"Mr. Chairman of the Board. My apologies for interrupting, but might I have the floor for a brief moment?"

Director Kim swallowed hard, casting a frantic, uneasy glance toward Chairman Kang before forcing a tight, nervous smile. "You... you have the floor, Director Kang."

The second permission was granted, Tae-soo reached into his suit jacket, producing a small velvet pouch and handing it down to Il-hyun.

Il-hyun tipped two deformed, mangled pieces of lead into his palm, raising them high above his head for the entire room to see.

Curious shareholders in the rear rows stretched their necks, some even standing from their seats to catch a glimpse of the shrapnel.

"These are the exact high-caliber rounds extracted from both of my thighs one week ago, on the day of my inauguration."

Wincing grimaces rippled through the suits as if they could feel the lead themselves. Il-hyun turned his hand slowly, displaying the flattened slugs to the left and right.

"What do you think? Must have hurt like absolute hell, wouldn't you say?"

The crude, vulgar phrasing drew a sharp scowl from Chairman Kang. Director Kim quickly leaned into his microphone. "Director Kang! This is an official corporate assembly. Mind your decorum."

Il-hyun ignored the reprimand entirely, his deep baritone carrying effortlessly across the silent room.

"And yet... while I lay bleeding out on a surgical table, a motion for my dismissal was drafted and submitted to this board."

"..."

"How exactly should I interpret this sequence of events, Director Kim?"

Il-hyun’s dark gaze locked dead-center onto Director Kim like a sniper's crosshairs.

Perched at the podium, Director Kim bristled with indignation, raising his voice to mask his panic. "What ridiculous insinuation are you making right now?!"

"I am merely asking whether the individual orchestrating my dismissal... might happen to be the very same person who put two bullets through my legs."

A violent murmur swept through the assembly. Director Kim slammed his palm onto the podium, his face flushing scarlet. "Cease this baseless slander at once!"

Il-hyun let out a chilling, melodious chuckle. "Baseless? Well... we shall see once the ballots are tallied whether my suspicions were truly baseless or not."

Director Kim gritted his teeth, glaring with venomous hatred.

Il-hyun remained utterly unfazed, casually sweeping his gaze across the assembly. Among the seated executives were several faces known to belong to the opposing camp. Looking at them, Il-hyun wore a bright, charming smile, though the malice burning in his dark irises looked ready to strip the flesh clean from their bones.

He raised his voice, calling out to his security chief:

"Tae-soo!"

"Yes, Director."

"Find the rat who pulled that trigger."

"Yes, sir."

"Once you drag him out... take a bone saw and sever every joint in his body, knuckle by knuckle."

A suffocating horror gripped the room, several board members turning stark white. Il-hyun flashed an ecstatic, predatory grin, delivering the final stroke:

"And feed the scraps to the dogs."

Chairman Kang could take no more. He slammed his cane against the floor and surged to his feet, wheeling around to face his son.

"You insolent bastard!"

Il-hyun tilted his head back, looking up at his father with cold, mocking insolence.

Foolish old monster. If you set out to murder me, you should have made damn sure I was dead.

"Why so furious, Father?" Il-hyun purred smoothly. "It’s not as if you were the one who hired the shooter."

As Chairman Kang’s face contorted in suppressed fury, Il-hyun suddenly winced, clutching his bandaged thighs with a sharp intake of breath.

The entire boardroom fell dead silent, not a single person daring to draw a breath.

Il-hyun looked around the frozen assembly, wearing a look of delicate, theatrical regret.

"My sincerest apologies, everyone. I wished to remain and participate in the democratic process, but it appears it is time for my scheduled morphine drip."

"..."

"I shall take my leave. Cast your votes wisely, gentlemen... and do take exceptionally good care of your health."

Flashing one last dazzling, bloodthirsty smile, the atmosphere in the room froze solid like a block of winter ice.

Chairman Kang stood trembling with white-hot rage, entirely powerless to stop him.

Il-hyun offered a lazy, mocking tip of his head, slid his dark sunglasses back over his eyes, and allowed Tae-soo to wheel him out of the boardroom in absolute triumph.
